citeAs: Lu, Pan, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, and Jianfeng Gao. (2024). MathVista: Evaluating Mathematical Reasoning of Foundation Models in Visual Contexts. ICLR 2024.
creator: Pan Lu, Hritik Bansal, Tony Xia, Jiacheng Liu, Chunyuan Li, Hannaneh Hajishirzi, Hao Cheng, Kai-Wei Chang, Michel Galley, Jianfeng Gao
description: MathVista is a benchmark for evaluating mathematical reasoning in visual contexts. It consists of 6,141 examples derived from 28 existing multimodal datasets and 3 newly created datasets, covering diverse mathematical reasoning types, tasks, and visual contexts.
name: MathVista
publisher: UCLA, University of Washington, Microsoft Research
rai:annotatorDemographics: Graduate students in STEM fields annotated the newly created datasets. Human evaluators for model baselines were qualified human annotators with a high school diploma or higher; Amazon Mechanical Turk annotators for human performance had completed more than 5,000 HIT tasks, had an acceptance score higher than 0.99, and were retained only if they had achieved a high school diploma or higher.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For the 736 newly collected questions, independent annotation by three reviewers resulted in a 99.2% inter-annotation consistency rate, with only 6 disagreements resolved through discussion. For labeling whether problems involve mathematical reasoning, the paper reports a Fleiss Kappa score of 0.775 among three annotators. For verification of automatic mathematical reasoning labels on 1,000 examples, 94.1% of examples had the exact same set of reasoning types between automatic and human annotations, and 98.79% of individual labels were identical.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For filtering VQA examples, heuristic rules first automatically selected candidates likely involving mathematical reasoning, and then three expert annotators manually labeled whether examples involved mathematical reasoning using majority voting. For the three new datasets, all questions were manually annotated by graduate students in STEM fields and refined through a rigorous review process; each dataset was independently annotated by three reviewers and disagreements were resolved through team discussion. Metadata such as question type, answer type, language, source, category, task, grade level, and visual context were obtained from source dataset details, and mathematical reasoning labels were automatically obtained then manually verified on 1,000 examples.
rai:dataBiases: The benchmark draws from heterogeneous source datasets and annotations sourced from original data providers, resulting in only 85.6% of examples having annotations and lacking a unified format and structure. The paper also notes there may be gaps in representation of certain mathematical problems and visual contexts, and that collecting high-quality data in these domains is labor-intensive, which may affect scalability and generalizability.
rai:dataCollection: MathVista was constructed by collecting 9 existing multimodal MathQA datasets, reviewing more than 70 VQA datasets and selecting 19 publicly available ones with math-related instances, and creating 3 new datasets: IQTest, FunctionQA, and PaperQA. The final benchmark includes 6,141 examples, with each source dataset limited to up to 400 examples for balanced representation.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw/source data consist of examples from 31 source datasets, including 9 existing MathQA datasets, 19 existing VQA datasets, and 3 newly annotated datasets. Newly created data include puzzle test figures from online learning platforms, functional plots, and academic paper figures such as tables, figures, and charts from online education resources and papers on Huggingface.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: PaperQA includes 107 examples sourced from papers released in August 2023 on Huggingface.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Others
rai:dataLimitations: The paper notes limitations in dataset coverage, with possible gaps in certain types of mathematical problems and visuals. It also states that only 85.6% of examples have annotations, and annotations from original data providers lack a unified format and structure because of source heterogeneity. The scalability and generalizability of the benchmark to other domains remain a concern.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: To balance source representation, each source dataset was limited to up to 400 examples. For creating the released subsets, the authors randomly sampled 4 questions from each source dataset and then randomly sampled remaining questions in proportion to each source dataset's representation in the whole benchmark.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For VQA datasets, heuristic rules automatically selected examples likely to involve mathematical reasoning by choosing examples with numeric answers or quantity words in the question. False positives were then removed through expert annotation. Each source dataset was capped at 400 examples for balance. For release preparation, the dataset was split into testmini and test, with testmini sampled by first randomly sampling 4 questions per source dataset and then sampling remaining questions proportionally to each source dataset's share in the full set. The authors also conducted several quality checks to address unidentified errors.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state that answer labels for the test split will not be publicly released and that they will maintain an online evaluation platform. They also state that the benchmark is part of an ongoing research process, and they are committed to maintaining the datasets, refining potential data noise in response to community feedback, and evolving the leaderboard in response to new models.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper positions MathVista as supporting the development of general-purpose AI agents capable of tackling mathematically intensive and visually rich real-world tasks, including educational disciplines, statistical analysis, theorem proving, and scientific discovery. It argues that the benchmark can help evaluate progress and reveal limitations of current models in these domains.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended to evaluate and benchmark foundation models, including large language models and large multimodal models, on mathematical reasoning in visual contexts, and to facilitate development of mathematical reasoning systems in visually intensive scenarios.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Heuristic rules were used to automatically select likely mathematical reasoning examples from VQA datasets. Automatic annotation was also used to obtain coarse labels of mathematical reasoning types, which were then manually verified. EasyOCR was used in the broader benchmarking pipeline for OCR text detection, and GPT-4 was used as an answer extractor in evaluation, but not as ground-truth dataset annotation tools.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes some questions involving people, such as age-gap questions about named individuals or celebrities, and contains 6.57% non-English questions including Chinese and Persian. No systematic collection of personal demographic, health, or other sensitive personal information for dataset subjects is described.
